messages:
incident-bot: [P0] control-plane -> data-plane propagation delay detected. Metric spike: controlplane.propagation_latency > 30s for 7m. Some console UI changes not reflected in API responses. Auto-paging oncall
Olivia N: taking initial sync. joining bridge now :phone:
Devon (oncall): I'm on the bridge, have the pager. Can someone paste a quick repro of the console vs API mismatch? Need an example to show on the timeline
Samir: AcmeCorp reported 500s on embed route and mismatched model config in console vs /v1/models. Quick check: console shows model "redwood-small-quantized:v2" for tenant acme-prod but API /v1/tenants/acme-prod/model returns "redwood-small-quantized:v1"
Kai: adding logs I just grabbed from control-plane (controller managers) 
Kai: ```
[2026-02-25T14:01:12Z] propagation-manager: enqueued update tenant=acme-prod version=v2
[2026-02-25T14:01:13Z] propagation-manager: push to queue shard=3 size=1
[2026-02-25T14:01:40Z] propagation-retry: transport timeout to dataplane-node-7, err=write: connection reset
[2026-02-25T14:03:01Z] propagation-manager: marked update as in-flight tenant=acme-prod seq=4321
```
Olivia N: thanks Kai. I can see retries to dataplane nodes around 14:01-14:03. Devon can you run a quick curl from inside the dataplane node to confirm what the API surface is returning?
Devon (oncall): running now on dataplane-node-7 (ssh). curl output:
Devon (oncall): ```
$ curl -sS https://api.internal/v1/tenants/acme-prod/model | jq .
{"model": "redwood-small-quantized:v1", "propagated_at": "2026-02-25T14:00:58Z"}
```
Maria Ops: console UI cache shows v2 because console reads from control-plane cache which was updated locally, but actual dataplane agent hasn't applied it. Hypothesis: propagation queue starved or transport auth failures intermittently between control-plane and dataplane.
Samir: I see two possible causes: 1) transport-level TLS renegotiation caused connection resets to some dataplane nodes (Kai's logs) 2) propagation manager backoff bug that stops retries after N failures but reports in-flight. Need to check propagation manager metrics: queued_count and retry_count per tenant
Olivia N: timeline so far (please add entries):
- 14:00:58Z control-plane marks v2 deployed for acme-prod
- 14:01:12Z propagation enqueue (Kai log)
- 14:01:40Z transport reset to dataplane-node-7
- 14:03:01Z propagation marked in-flight (Kai)
- 14:04:10Z first customer error spike observed (ingest metrics)
- 14:05:00Z incident-bot alerted on propagation_latency > 30s
Devon (oncall): I'm pulling dataplane agent logs now. Running: kubectl logs -l role=dataplane-agent -n prod --since=30m | grep acme-prod -n
Devon (oncall): snippet: ```
[2026-02-25T14:00:55Z] agent: recv update tenant=acme-prod seq=4321
[2026-02-25T14:01:41Z] agent: apply failed: write tcp 10.1.7.12:443->10.2.9.8:54718: connection reset by peer
[2026-02-25T14:02:10Z] agent: retrying apply tenant=acme-prod attempt=3
[2026-02-25T14:03:20Z] agent: apply succeeded tenant=acme-prod seq=4321
```
Samir: Interesting — dataplane retried and later succeeded at 14:03:20Z but error spike started at 14:04+, suggests partial propagation across region or some nodes still stale. Need to check sharding: which nodes serve acme-prod traffic?
Kai: running query against routing table: acme-prod served by dataplane-node-{3,7,12} in us-west. Node-7 was slow to apply, node-3 applied immediately. Node-12 shows no apply entry after 14:03 in agent logs.
Maria Ops: customer impact assessment: affecting 12% of acme-prod requests (error code 503 from model mismatch) between 14:04-14:11; topline SLO churn visible. Need mitigation to reduce blast radius.
Olivia N: mitigation options: 1) force repropagate to all nodes with admin API 2) rollback control-plane config to v1 for acme-prod 3) route acme-prod traffic away from nodes with stale config (weight 0)
Devon (oncall): I'll try option 1 first: POST /admin/propagate?tenant=acme-prod&force=true from control-plane. Executing now.
Devon (oncall): ```
$ http POST https://control-plane.internal/admin/propagate tenant==acme-prod force==true -v
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
{"job_id":"prop-20260225-183"}
```
incident-bot: propagation job prop-20260225-183 queued to shards {3,7,12}
Kai: pushing a temporary mitigation: increase propagation concurrency to avoid retry backoff clog. Patching config: 
Kai: ```bash
kubectl -n control-plane set env deployment/propagation-manager MAX_IN_FLIGHT=50
kubectl rollout restart deploy/propagation-manager -n control-plane
```
Olivia N: please monitor metrics after the restart — propagation_latency, queued_count, retry_count. Also patch oncall runbook to capture if propagation restarts cause extra load on dataplane
Devon (oncall): propagation-manager rolled, job prop-20260225-183 progressed: node-12 applied at 14:06:08Z, node-7 applied at 14:06:14Z
Devon (oncall): dataplane agent logs now show consistent applies 
Devon (oncall): ```
[2026-02-25T14:06:08Z] agent: apply succeeded tenant=acme-prod seq=4321 node=12
[2026-02-25T14:06:14Z] agent: apply succeeded tenant=acme-prod seq=4321 node=7
```
Maria Ops: customer errors dropped to 1.2% by 14:07, continuing to trend down. Marking immediate mitigation success.
Samir: still need root cause: why did node-12 not apply earlier while node-3 did? Two leads: intermittent network blips to node-12 (routing) or per-node agent bug where apply acknowledgment dropped. Can we get tcpdump for node-12?
Kai: grabbing tcpdump; will upload pcap to incident artifacts. Also found TLS renegotiation error in node-12 kernel logs around 14:01:40Z. Attaching excerpt: 
Kai: ```
Feb 25 14:01:40 host kernel: [NET] TLS: unexpected renegotiation from 10.0.2.7
```
Olivia N: good. Hypothesis ranking: 1) network/TLS renegotiation causing propagation outages to subset of nodes (high) 2) propagation-manager backoff combined with partial success causing drift (medium) 3) agent apply ack loss (low).
Devon (oncall): action items for RCA: collect propagation-manager metrics (queued_count, retry_count), agent ack logs for nodes 3/7/12, network captures for node-12, and list of tenants affected. I'll own immediate artifacts and timeline.
Maria Ops: I'll handle customer comms: draft status update to AcmeCorp and internal CSMs. Recommend mention limited impact window and mitigation steps taken.
Samir: note for post-incident: add heartbeat/ack guarantee to propagation protocol (persist ack to control-plane before marking applied) and add per-node health routing to avoid serving from stale nodes during propagation windows.
Olivia N: agree. After-action items: Maria Ops (comm), Devon (artifacts+timeline), Samir (propagation protocol follow-up), Kai (network team liaison). Owner for RCA doc: Maria Ops. Expected RCA draft in 72h.
Maria Ops: creating incident ticket and assigning owners now. Ticket: INC-20260225-712.
incident-bot: bridge closed (duration 34m). Incident severity: P0 -> mitigated. Please follow up in INC-20260225-712 for RCA and postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
